tools_problematic.problem: Not a valid winapp CLI subcommand — it does not exist. Following the SKILL.md instruction to run a 'final winapp build' produced a hard failure.
tools_problematic.evidence: session-log.txt L3742-3773: `winapp build` -> "'build' was not matched" + full winapp usage dump, WINAPP_BUILD_EXIT=1 (exit code 1). winapp's own help lists init/restore/update/package/sign/cert/manifest/create-debug-identity/run/ui — no `build`.

tool_limitations.limitation: winapp compiles nothing; it is a packaging/identity/run/UI-automation CLI (SKILL.md L14 even says so). There is no `winapp build`.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Change SKILL.md/MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md to instruct `dotnet build` (with an exit sentinel) for compilation and reserve `winapp` for run/packaging only.

doc_errors.wrong: Instructs the agent to run `winapp build` to compile the project ('compile; never run the .exe directly' / 'Prefer winapp build to compile' / 'do a final winapp build').
doc_errors.correct: Compilation is done with `dotnet build` (native SDK build). `winapp` has no `build` subcommand; use `dotnet build -c Debug -p:Platform=<arch>; "BUILD_EXIT=$LASTEXITCODE"`.

doc_errors.wrong: Refers to 'The benchmark's `winapp build` injects the Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK.Analyzers package'.
doc_errors.correct: The analyzer package is injected by the WindowsAppSDK NuGet reference at `dotnet build` time, not by a nonexistent `winapp build`.

special_apis.special_handling: Pure WinRT runtime API with no XAML surface; ported verbatim (GetForecast() on a background thread via Task.Run, ForecastUpdated event). No migration change needed — it is available to WinUI 3 desktop as-is. Empty forecast on the build machine is the genuine runtime outcome, not a defect.

errors_encountered.error: `winapp build` -> "'build' was not matched. ... Unrecognized command or argument 'build'", exit 1
errors_encountered.root_cause: SKILL.md instructs a winapp subcommand that does not exist; winapp is a packaging/run/UI CLI, not a compiler.
errors_encountered.fix: Agent fell back to `dotnet build -c Debug -p:Platform=<arch>; "BUILD_EXIT=$LASTEXITCODE"` (session-log.txt L3778), which built cleanly.

dev_agent_struggles.where: Final build step (Step 4 close-out), session-log.txt L3742-3778
dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Ran `winapp build` per SKILL.md; it errored out (exit 1) with a full usage dump.
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: SKILL.md hard-codes `winapp build` as the compile command in three places, but winapp has no build verb.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent recognized the invalid command and re-ran with `dotnet build`.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Fix SKILL.md/MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md to use `dotnet build` for compilation everywhere `winapp build` currently appears.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: First invocation of Validate-UwpMigration.ps1 used the path `<Target>\.github\skills\...` (script located under the project subfolder) which did not exist; "term ... is not recognized".
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: 1 retry (TURN 20->21) before finding the copy at `<app>\.github\skills\...`
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The scaffold copies the skill into the app tree; the agent guessed the script sat under -Target rather than at the app root. SKILL.md uses a `<skill-root>` placeholder, so the general instruction is correct.
dev_agent_struggles.how_resolved: Agent corrected the path in one retry.
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Minor; SKILL.md already uses `<skill-root>` distinct from `-Target`. Treated as a dev-agent slip, not a skill change.
